mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week improvement in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks, despite a slight slowdown in the most recent week, indicates a sustained underlying trend of increasing public engagement with retail and recreation venues, which will continue over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility in the most recent week, following a period of improvement, suggests a renewed caution or reduction in essential outings. This reduction in general public movement will spill over into reduced discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decrease or shows an increase in the next two weeks following a similar drop in GROCERY_PHARM, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The significant drop in PARKS mobility in the most recent week, after a period of strong recovery, indicates a general reduction in outdoor discretionary movement. This could be due to weather changes or renewed public health concerns, which will negatively impact overall retail and recreation over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases in the week following a similar sharp decline in PARKS mobility, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The continued gradual increase in WORKPLACES mobility combined with a sustained, albeit slowly decreasing, elevation in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a hybrid work model is becoming established. failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines while WORKPLACES continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, or if WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL trends decouple without RETAIL_REC increasing, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The steady, albeit slow, recovery in TRANSIT mobility, coupled with the improving trend in RETAIL_REC itself, indicates increasing confidence in public spaces and transportation. This synergy will further accelerate the recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as more people use transit for discretionary trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility continues to improve week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility improves but RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next two weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In the early stages of reopening, an initial surge in outdoor activities (PARKS) often precedes a shift towards indoor retail and recreation as more establishments become fully operational and public confidence grows. The recent drop in PARKS mobility may signal this shift, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility declines after a period of strong recovery
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility declines but RETAIL_REC also declines or remains stagnant over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% baseline change
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% but RETAIL_REC shows a strong and sustained increase over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -30% baseline change
